docs.title: Open Observability Results Standard (OORS)
docs.text:
The Open Observability Results Standard (OORS) is a lightweight, tool-agnostic format for exchanging data quality and data observability results.

An OORS message reports the outcomes of checks and metrics — pass/fail, measured values, threshold breaches — optionally linked to the data contract (ODCS/ODPS) that specified them. It deliberately does not carry raw metrics, traces, or logs.

docs.title: WORK IN PROGRESS — NOT READY FOR PRODUCTION
docs.text: OORS is a draft standard (v0.8.0), published early so the community can see it and shape it. It is not a released standard. Expect breaking changes in every version until v1.0.0, and incomplete areas. Do not build production systems against it.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Fundamentals — the message envelope (apiVersion, kind, id, observedAt) plus the source and optional contract objects.
  • Results — the structure of an individual observation (check or metric).
  • Run Lifecycle — terminal by default, progressive by choice: the optional run object for long-running executions.
  • Custom & Other Properties — extending OORS with customProperties.
  • Tags — lightweight, free-form classification labels for the message and its results.
  • Variables — ${VAR_NAME} interpolation for environment-specific values, resolved at runtime by tooling.
  • Examples — complete OORS messages.

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text:
• Lightweight — a flat, concise structure; easy to print, log, send over HTTP, or push to a queue.
  • Tool-agnostic — can wrap results from OpenTelemetry, vendor tools, ETL pipelines, custom applications, or ad-hoc scripts.
  • Contract-aware — optional, first-class linkage to ODCS/ODPS IDs so data products can expose their health consistently.
  • Result-centric — carries only the outcomes of checks (pass/fail, measured values, breaches), not raw metrics or traces.

OORS is defined by RFC-0018, approved by the TSC on 2026-10-14, and is part of the Bitol family of standards, alongside ODCS and ODPS.

docs.title: Changelog: Open Observability Results Standard (OORS)
docs.text: This document tracks the history and evolution of the Open Observability Results Standard.

docs.title: v0.8.0 - DRAFT
docs.text:
• Approves RFC-0018 — Open Observability Results Standard, the founding RFC, approved by the TSC on 2026-10-14. OORS is no longer an implementation of an open draft: it is now the formal consequence of an approved RFC.
  • Adds optional contract.server — the identifier of the server, as defined in the referenced contract (e.g., the server name in the ODCS servers section), against which the observations were made. A contract can be served on multiple servers (e.g., production, dev); this field records which one the results apply to. Non-breaking: the field is optional. Recreates the contribution made in #8 by @jochenchrist on top of v0.8.0.
  • Adds tags — the shared Bitol structure for free-form classification labels (an array of strings), available at the top level and on each result. See the new Tags page. Non-breaking: the field is optional.
  • Extends results[].status to the five outcomes the RFC defines: pass, fail, warn (executed, breached a soft/warning threshold), error (could not be evaluated — verdict unknown; e.g. the query failed or the source was unreachable) and skip (intentionally not run). The schema previously permitted only pass and fail. error is deliberately distinct from fail: a failure is a known-bad verdict, an error is the absence of a verdict and must not be counted as a failure. Non-breaking — this widens an enum. See Status values.
  • Documents severity as orthogonal to status: status is the runtime outcome, severity is the definition-time importance of the check. The two compose — a critical-severity check with status: error is the loudest possible alert.
  • Default apiVersion raised to v0.8.0.
  • New statuses example (YAML + JSON) exercising all five outcomes, and the first negative-test fixtures under tests/negative/ — invalid documents the schema must reject — wired into scripts/validate-examples.sh.
  • New Tags documentation page, mirroring the ODCS page; Custom & Other Properties restructured to align with ODCS. The full example gains contract.server and tags.

docs.title: v0.2.2 - DRAFT
docs.text:
• Renames source.runID to source.runId and contract.contractID to contract.contractId, following the Bitol camel-case naming convention. Breaking: source and contract set additionalProperties: false, so documents still using runID or contractID no longer validate against the v0.2.2 schema.
  • Default apiVersion raised to v0.2.2.

docs.title: v0.2.1 - DRAFT
docs.text:
• Adds optional top-level run object — run lifecycle reporting: terminal by default, progressive by choice. A document without run (every pre-v0.2.1 document) is terminal: the authoritative record of its run. Producers of long-running executions can opt in to interim snapshots with run.state: running, plus optional run.sequence (monotonic ordering per source.runID) and run.progress (current/total/unit). run.state: completed|aborted marks a terminal document; a terminal document supersedes all interim documents sharing its source.runID. source.runID is required (schema-enforced) when run.state is running. results[].status semantics are unchanged — lifecycle is orthogonal to observation outcomes. See the new Run Lifecycle page.
  • Default apiVersion raised to v0.2.1.
  • New progressive example (YAML + JSON); full example extended with the run object.

docs.title: v0.2.0 - DRAFT
docs.text:
• Adds customProperties — a list of key/value pairs (shared structure across the Bitol standards: property, value, optional description and id) at the top level and on each result, for vendor- or organization-specific extensions.
  • Adds optional vendor string on customProperties items, associating a custom property with a specific vendor, provider, or external system. SHOULD be a stable, lowercase identifier (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$); not enforced, and tools MUST preserve unknown vendor values — RFC 0035, shared with ODCS v3.2.0 and ODPS v1.1.0 (slated for OORS v1.0.0).
  • Adds relatesTo on result objects — an optional reference to the element this result relates to in the linked contract (e.g., a path to a data quality rule or property in the referenced ODCS/ODPS contract).
  • Adds variable interpolation — any string value MAY contain ${VAR_NAME} references resolved at runtime by tooling, with the POSIX ${VAR_NAME:-default} form for inline defaults. Tools MUST resolve references before use, MUST NOT silently substitute empty strings, and MUST preserve unresolved tokens verbatim on round-trip. No new section or field — RFC 0050, shared with ODCS v3.2.0 and ODPS v1.1.0 (slated for OORS v1.0.0).
  • Default apiVersion raised to v0.2.0.
  • Documentation expanded to match the ODCS/ODPS structure: per-section pages with front matter, a table-of-contents landing page, and a Custom & Other Properties page.

docs.title: v0.1.0 - DRAFT
docs.text:
Initial draft of the Open Observability Results Standard, based on RFC-0018.

  • Top-level fundamentals: apiVersion, kind (ObservabilityResults), id, observedAt.
  • source object: process (required), runID, vendor.
  • Optional contract object linking results to an ODCS/ODPS contract: contractID, standard, version.
  • results array (at least one) of result objects, each with id, type (check/metric), name, status (pass/fail), and optional severity, dimension, target (resourceType, resourceIdentifier), measure (metric, value, threshold, unit), and message.
  • JSON Schema (oors-json-schema-v0.1.0.json) and example messages.

docs.title: Contributing to Open Observability Results Standard
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to Open Observability Results Standard (OORS). Please refer to the TSC contributing guidelines.

docs.title: Branching and merging
docs.text:
main is protected by a repository rule that requires changes to land through a pull request — direct pushes to main are rejected.

Reviews are not required. Any TSC member with write access can merge their own pull request immediately; a second reviewer is welcome but never a gate. main cannot be force-pushed or deleted.

The validate-examples workflow runs on every pull request and verifies the examples against the schema. It is advisory: a red run should be understood, not ignored.

Documentation is published automatically from main to https://bitol-io.github.io/open-observability-results-standard/.

docs.title: Custom & Other Properties
docs.text:
This section covers other properties you may find in an OORS message.

Back to TOC

docs.title: Custom Properties
docs.text: This section covers custom properties you can use to add non-standard properties. This block is available at the top level of an OORS message and on each result. The structure is shared across the Bitol standards and follows the same shape as ODCS custom properties.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
customProperties:
  - id: rfc_ruleset_name
    property: refRulesetName
    value: gcsc.ruleset.name
  - property: orchestrator
    value: airflow
    description: Cluster name for specific applications
  - property: catalogId
    value: cat-987
    vendor: zeenea

{
  "customProperties": [
    {
      "id": "rfc_ruleset_name",
      "property": "refRulesetName",
      "value": "gcsc.ruleset.name"
    },
    {
      "property": "orchestrator",
      "value": "airflow",
      "description": "Cluster name for specific applications"
    },
    {
      "property": "catalogId",
      "value": "cat-987",
      "vendor": "zeenea"
    }
  ]
}

Custom properties can equally be attached to an individual result:

results:
  - id: completeness_customer_email
    type: check
    name: customer email completeness
    status: pass
    customProperties:
      - property: checkEngine
        value: soda-core

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text: Key Type UX label Required Description customProperties array Custom Properties No A list of key/value pairs for custom properties. customProperties[].description string Description No Description for humans. customProperties[].id string ID No A unique identifier for the element used to create stable, refactor-safe references. Recommended for elements that will be referenced. customProperties[].property string Property Yes The name of the key. Names should be in camel case—the same as if they were permanent properties in the standard. customProperties[].value any Value Yes The value of the key. It can be an array. customProperties[].vendor string Vendor No Identifies the vendor, provider, or external system associated with this custom property. SHOULD be a stable, lowercase identifier matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ (e.g. confluent, zeenea). Tools MUST preserve unknown vendor values. (Added in v0.2.0, RFC 0035.)

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Tags are lightweight, free-form classification labels that can be attached to the message and to individual results. See the dedicated Tags page.

docs.title: Other Properties
docs.text: This section covers other properties you may find in an OORS message.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: v0.8.0
kind: ObservabilityResults

docs.title: Other properties definition
docs.text:
Key Type UX label Required Description apiVersion string API Version Yes Version of the OORS schema used. See Fundamentals. kind string Kind Yes The type of OORS object. For OORS, always ObservabilityResults.

Back to TOC

docs.title: Fundamentals
docs.text:
The top level of an OORS message describes when and by what the observations were made, optionally which contract they relate to, and carries the list of results.

Any string value MAY contain ${VAR_NAME} references resolved at runtime by tooling; see Variables.

Back to TOC

docs.title: Minimal
docs.text:
Only the required fields: the envelope, source.process, and one result.

apiVersion: v0.8.0
kind: ObservabilityResults
id: 9f1c8a52-2b4e-4a6e-9d3e-7c2a1f0b4d11
observedAt: "2026-01-15T09:30:00Z"
source:
  process: nightly-quality-suite
results:
  - id: no_dup_rows
    type: check
    name: No duplicate rows
    status: pass

{
  "apiVersion": "v0.8.0",
  "kind": "ObservabilityResults",
  "id": "9f1c8a52-2b4e-4a6e-9d3e-7c2a1f0b4d11",
  "observedAt": "2026-01-15T09:30:00Z",
  "source": {
    "process": "nightly-quality-suite"
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "no_dup_rows",
      "type": "check",
      "name": "No duplicate rows",
      "status": "pass"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Full
docs.text:
A full envelope: source with all fields, a run lifecycle object, a contract reference (including the server it is served on), results, tags, and customProperties. (See Results for the result fields and Run Lifecycle for run.) The complete files are in examples/.

apiVersion: v0.8.0
kind: ObservabilityResults
id: 3d2b6e90-7a1c-4f5b-8e2d-1a9c4b6f0e23
observedAt: "2026-01-15T09:30:00Z"
source:
  process: order-processor-dbt
  runId: build-4821
  vendor: soda
run:
  state: completed
contract:
  contractId: 53581432-6c55-4ba2-a65f-72344a91553a
  standard: ODCS
  version: 3.1.0
  server: production
results:
  - id: dup_rows_myTable
    type: check
    name: No duplicate rows
    status: fail
  - id: freshness_myDataProduct
    type: metric
    name: Data should not be stale
    status: pass
tags: ['finance', 'sox']
customProperties:
  - property: environment
    value: production

{
  "apiVersion": "v0.8.0",
  "kind": "ObservabilityResults",
  "id": "3d2b6e90-7a1c-4f5b-8e2d-1a9c4b6f0e23",
  "observedAt": "2026-01-15T09:30:00Z",
  "source": {
    "process": "order-processor-dbt",
    "runId": "build-4821",
    "vendor": "soda"
  },
  "run": { "state": "completed" },
  "contract": {
    "contractId": "53581432-6c55-4ba2-a65f-72344a91553a",
    "standard": "ODCS",
    "version": "3.1.0",
    "server": "production"
  },
  "results": [
    { "id": "dup_rows_myTable", "type": "check", "name": "No duplicate rows", "status": "fail" },
    { "id": "freshness_myDataProduct", "type": "metric", "name": "Data should not be stale", "status": "pass" }
  ],
  "tags": ["finance", "sox"],
  "customProperties": [
    { "property": "environment", "value": "production" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text:
Key Type UX label Required Description Example apiVersion string API Version Yes Version of the OORS schema used. v0.8.0 kind string Kind Yes The type of OORS object. For OORS, always ObservabilityResults. ObservabilityResults id string (UUID) ID Yes A unique identifier (could be a UUID) identifying the observability results. 9f1c8a52-2b4e-4a6e-9d3e-7c2a1f0b4d11 observedAt string (ISO 8601) Observed At Yes The moment in time when the observations were done (ISO 8601 format). 2026-01-15T09:30:00Z source object Source Yes Object describing the source from where the results come (e.g., job, pipeline). source.process string Process Yes The name of the process (job, pipeline, etc.) that made the observations. order-processor-dbt source.runId string Run ID No An optional unique identifier for the specific run/execution of the process. build-4821 source.vendor string Vendor No An optional field indicating the vendor or tool that produced the observations. soda run object Run No Run lifecycle object. Absent ⇒ the document is terminal. See Run Lifecycle. contract object Contract No Object describing the contract that provided the specifications for the observations. Highly recommended for traceability. contract.contractId string (UUID) Contract ID No A unique identifier identifying the specific contract (ODCS/ODPS) the observations are based on. 53581432-6c55-4ba2-a65f-72344a91553a contract.standard string Standard No The standard followed by the contract. ODCS contract.version string Version No The version of the contract (not the standard). 3.1.0 contract.server string Server No The identifier of the server, as defined in the referenced contract (e.g., the server name in the ODCS servers section), against which the observations were made. A contract can be served on multiple servers; this field records which one the results apply to. production results array Results Yes An array of results (at least one). Each entry is a result object (check or metric). tags array Tags No A list of tags for categorizing the message. See Tags. ['finance', 'sox'] customProperties array Custom Properties No A list of key/value pairs for custom properties. See Custom & Other Properties.

Note: When a contract is provided, all observations in results are expected to be based on the specifications defined in that contract. Observations not related to the contract should be sent in separate OORS messages (without the contract object).

Note: An OORS document is terminal by default — without a run object it is the authoritative record of the run that produced it. Long-running producers can opt in to progressive reporting with the optional run object; see Run Lifecycle.

docs.title: Open Observability Results Standard (OORS)
docs.text:
The Open Observability Results Standard (OORS) provides an easy, lightweight mechanism to exchange data quality and data observability results across systems.

OORS focuses on clarity, portability, and ease of implementation, letting teams communicate operational outcomes — such as data quality checks, freshness, latency, and SLA breaches — without requiring deep observability expertise or complex infrastructure. As an open format developed within the Bitol community, OORS is human-readable and follows the same philosophy as ODCS and ODPS, integrating naturally into existing data workflows.

docs.title: WORK IN PROGRESS — NOT READY FOR PRODUCTION
docs.text: OORS is a draft standard, published early so the community can see it and shape it. It is not a released standard. Expect breaking changes in every version until v1.0.0, and incomplete areas. Do not build production systems against it.

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text:
• Lightweight — a flat, concise structure; easy to print, log, send over HTTP, or push to a queue.
  • Tool-agnostic — can wrap results from OpenTelemetry, vendor tools, ETL pipelines, custom applications, or ad-hoc scripts.
  • Contract-aware — optional, first-class linkage to ODCS/ODPS IDs so data products can expose their health consistently.
  • Result-centric — carries only the outcomes of checks (pass/fail, measured values, breaches), not raw metrics or traces.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Fundamentals — the top-level structure of an OORS message.
  • Results — the structure of an individual result.
  • Examples — sample OORS messages.

The JSON Schema lives in schema/. Files using the .oors.yaml extension are auto-detected as OORS.

A reader-friendly version of the standard will be available on its dedicated site once OORS is released publicly.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: v0.8.0
kind: ObservabilityResults
id: 9f1c8a52-2b4e-4a6e-9d3e-7c2a1f0b4d11
observedAt: "2025-12-25T17:00:00+01:00"
source:
  process: order-preprocessor-dbt
  runId: "27a3de3d"
  vendor: inhouse-build
results:
  - id: dup_rows_myTable
    type: check
    name: No duplicate rows
    status: fail
    severity: critical
    dimension: uniqueness
    target:
      resourceType: table
      resourceIdentifier: myTable
    measure:
      metric: rowCount
      value: 3
      threshold:
        mustBe: 0
      unit: rows
    message: Multiple duplicate rows found in myTable!

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: OORS is governed by the Bitol Technical Steering Committee (TSC). See contributing.md and the TSC contributing guidelines. The defining RFC is RFC-0018 (OORS), approved by the TSC on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Each entry in the results array is a single observation — either a check (a pass/fail assertion) or a metric (a measured value). A check reports a pass/fail outcome; a metric reports a measured value (its status still indicates whether the value met expectations).

Back to TOC

docs.title: Minimal
docs.text:
A result requires only id, type, name, and status.

- id: no_dup_rows
  type: check
  name: No duplicate rows
  status: pass

{
  "id": "no_dup_rows",
  "type": "check",
  "name": "No duplicate rows",
  "status": "pass"
}

docs.title: Full
docs.text:
A result using every field — a failing check linked to a contract rule via relatesTo, with a target, a measured value against a threshold, a message, and custom properties.

- id: dup_rows_myTable
  type: check
  name: No duplicate rows
  status: fail
  relatesTo: schema/orders_tbl/quality/dq_no_duplicates
  severity: critical
  dimension: uniqueness
  target:
    resourceType: table
    resourceIdentifier: myTable
  measure:
    metric: rowCount
    value: 3
    threshold:
      mustBe: 0
    unit: rows
  message: Multiple duplicate rows found in myTable!
  tags: ['critical-path', 'uniqueness']
  customProperties:
    - property: checkEngine
      value: soda-core

{
  "id": "dup_rows_myTable",
  "type": "check",
  "name": "No duplicate rows",
  "status": "fail",
  "relatesTo": "schema/orders_tbl/quality/dq_no_duplicates",
  "severity": "critical",
  "dimension": "uniqueness",
  "target": {
    "resourceType": "table",
    "resourceIdentifier": "myTable"
  },
  "measure": {
    "metric": "rowCount",
    "value": 3,
    "threshold": {
      "mustBe": 0
    },
    "unit": "rows"
  },
  "message": "Multiple duplicate rows found in myTable!",
  "tags": ["critical-path", "uniqueness"],
  "customProperties": [
    {
      "property": "checkEngine",
      "value": "soda-core"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text: Key Type UX label Required Description Example id string Result ID Yes A unique identifier for the specific check/metric. dup_rows_myTable type string Type Yes The type of observation: check (pass/fail) or metric (measured value). check name string Name Yes A human-readable name for the check/metric. No duplicate rows status string Status Yes The outcome of the observation: pass, fail, warn, error, or skip. See Status values. fail relatesTo string Relates To No A reference to the element this result relates to in the linked contract (e.g., a path to a data quality rule or property). schema/orders_tbl/quality/dq_no_duplicates severity string Severity No The severity level, e.g., critical, high, medium, low, warning. Orthogonal to status: status is the runtime outcome, severity is the definition-time importance. critical dimension string Dimension No The data quality dimension (following ODCS data quality dimensions), e.g., accuracy, completeness, timeliness, uniqueness. uniqueness target object Target No Object describing the resource being observed. target.resourceType string Resource Type No The type of resource, e.g., table, column, dataset. table target.resourceIdentifier string / array Resource Identifier No The identifier(s) of the resource — a single string or an array of strings. myTable measure object Measure No Object describing the measurement details. measure.metric string Metric No The name of the metric being measured, e.g., rowCount, age, latency. rowCount measure.value number / string Value No The observed value of the metric. 3 measure.threshold object Threshold No The threshold criteria, e.g., mustBe, mustBeLessThan (following ODCS operator definitions). { "mustBe": 0 } measure.unit string Unit No The unit of measurement, e.g., rows, seconds, percent. rows message string Message No A human-readable message providing additional context about the observation. Multiple duplicate rows found! tags array Tags No A list of tags for categorizing the result. See Tags. ['critical-path'] customProperties array Custom Properties No A list of key/value pairs for custom properties. See Custom & Other Properties.

docs.title: Status values
docs.text:
status separates a known-bad verdict from the absence of a verdict:

Value Meaning pass Executed, met expectation. fail Executed, breached a hard threshold. warn Executed, breached a soft/warning threshold — alert, but do not fail a gate. error Could not be evaluated — verdict unknown (e.g. the query failed, or the source was unreachable). skip Intentionally not run (filtered out, disabled, or an unmet precondition).

error is deliberately distinct from fail: a failure is a known-bad verdict, an error is the absence of a verdict and must not be counted as a failure. Counting an infrastructure error as a data failure poisons dashboards and triggers the wrong remediation. Likewise, a skip must not read as either a pass or a fail.

severity is orthogonal to status and composes with it — a critical-severity check with status: error is the loudest possible alert, because the check you most care about could not even run.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
- id: dup_rows_myTable
  type: check
  name: No duplicate rows
  status: fail
- id: freshness_myDataProduct
  type: metric
  name: Data should not be stale
  status: warn
- id: schema_conformance_orders
  type: check
  name: Orders conform to the contract schema
  status: error
  severity: critical
- id: pii_scan_orders
  type: check
  name: No PII in the orders extract
  status: skip

docs.title: Run Lifecycle
docs.text:
An OORS document is terminal by default: without a run object, the document is the authoritative record of the run that produced it — exactly the pre-v0.2.1 semantics. Producers of long-running executions (multi-step pipelines, large batch jobs) can opt in to progressive reporting by adding the run object and emitting interim snapshots while the run is still going.

Back to TOC

docs.title: Interim snapshot
docs.text:
A pipeline that has completed step 12 of 14 reports the step's observation and marks the document as an interim snapshot of a running execution. source.runId is required so consumers can correlate the documents of one run.

apiVersion: v0.8.0
kind: ObservabilityResults
id: 1c40b98e-5a7d-4d2e-9f31-8b6c2e0a4f77
observedAt: "2026-07-07T20:15:51Z"
source:
  process: imdb-silver
  runId: silver-1783398037701
run:
  state: running
  sequence: 12
  progress:
    current: 12
    total: 14
    unit: steps
results:
  - id: rows_title_alias
    type: metric
    name: title_alias
    status: pass
    dimension: volume
    target:
      resourceType: table
      resourceIdentifier: title_alias
    measure:
      metric: rows_loaded
      value: 58518276
      unit: rows

{
  "apiVersion": "v0.8.0",
  "kind": "ObservabilityResults",
  "id": "1c40b98e-5a7d-4d2e-9f31-8b6c2e0a4f77",
  "observedAt": "2026-07-07T20:15:51Z",
  "source": {
    "process": "imdb-silver",
    "runId": "silver-1783398037701"
  },
  "run": {
    "state": "running",
    "sequence": 12,
    "progress": { "current": 12, "total": 14, "unit": "steps" }
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "rows_title_alias",
      "type": "metric",
      "name": "title_alias",
      "status": "pass",
      "dimension": "volume",
      "target": { "resourceType": "table", "resourceIdentifier": "title_alias" },
      "measure": { "metric": "rows_loaded", "value": 58518276, "unit": "rows" }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Terminal document
docs.text:
The same run's final document — state: completed (or simply no run object at all) — carries the full summary and supersedes every interim snapshot with the same source.runId.

apiVersion: v0.8.0
kind: ObservabilityResults
id: efa58843-12ec-418b-963d-40dda853f856
observedAt: "2026-07-07T20:43:31Z"
source:
  process: imdb-silver
  runId: silver-1783398037701
run:
  state: completed
  sequence: 15
  progress:
    current: 14
    total: 14
    unit: steps
results:
  - id: run
    type: check
    name: Silver build run
    status: pass

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text: Key Type UX label Required Description Example run object Run No Run lifecycle object. Absent ⇒ the document is terminal (authoritative record of the run — the pre-v0.2.1 behavior). run.state string State Yes (in run) running — interim snapshot, more documents will follow for this source.runId. completed — terminal, the run finished. aborted — terminal, the run ended before producing its full results. running run.sequence integer Sequence No Monotonically increasing ordinal of this document within the run. Consumers SHOULD order by sequence when present, falling back to observedAt. 12 run.progress object Progress No Progress indicator for the run. run.progress.current number Current Yes (in progress) The amount of progress made so far, e.g., steps completed. 12 run.progress.total number Total No The total amount expected, e.g., total steps. Omit when unknown. 14 run.progress.unit string Unit No The unit of progress, e.g., steps, tables, files, percent. steps

docs.title: Semantics
docs.text:
1. Terminal by default. A document without a run object, or with run.state of completed or aborted, is terminal: the authoritative record for its source.runId. Every pre-v0.2.1 document is therefore already valid and terminal — nothing to migrate.
  2. Interim snapshots. A document with run.state: running is a partial snapshot of a run still in progress. Consumers MUST NOT treat it as the run's outcome. source.runId is required on interim documents (enforced by the JSON schema) so they can be correlated.
  3. Supersession. A terminal document supersedes all interim documents sharing its source.runId. The run's outcome is derived from the terminal document's results (its pass/fail checks) — run.state describes the lifecycle, not the quality outcome. aborted means only "no full summary is coming"; producers SHOULD still include a failing check describing why when they can.
  4. Observations stand alone. Each result in an interim document is a real observation that individually passed or failed — results[].status keeps its exact meaning. No new status values are introduced.
  5. Ordering. Consumers SHOULD order a run's documents by run.sequence when present, falling back to observedAt. Producers SHOULD make sequence strictly increasing per runId.

Consumer guidance (non-normative): a run whose latest document says running and that has produced no new document for an implementation-defined window may be rendered as stale — the wire format deliberately carries no heartbeat or timeout.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags are lightweight, free-form classification labels that can be attached to an OORS message and to individual results. The structure is shared across the Bitol standards and follows the same shape everywhere it appears.

Back to TOC

docs.title: What tags are for
docs.text:
Tags are intended for categorization — making observations easier to find, filter, group, and route through tooling. Common uses include:

  • Domain or topic: finance, marketing, iot
  • Sensitivity / compliance: pii, phi, gdpr, pci, sensitive
  • Lifecycle: experimental, deprecated, terminal
  • Audience: internal, external, partner
  • Operational hint: hot, cold, archive

Tags are deliberately not a controlled vocabulary: your organisation defines what each tag means. For vendor- or organisation-specific metadata that carries a value rather than a label, prefer custom properties.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A tags value is always an array of strings. Empty arrays are allowed; duplicate strings within the same array should be avoided.

tags: ['finance', 'sensitive']

The same structure applies wherever tags is permitted.

docs.title: Where tags can appear
docs.text:
tags is available in the following places:

Location Notes Top-level (the message) Tags applied to the observation run as a whole. See Fundamentals. Result Tags applied to an individual check/metric. See Results.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Lowercase, snake_case or single words. Mixed casing makes filtering brittle.
  • Be consistent. A tag pii in one message and PII in another defeats the purpose. Document your tag taxonomy organisation-wide.
  • Prefer specific over generic. customer_pii is more useful than sensitive once you have many messages.
  • Avoid encoding hierarchy in tag strings. finance/regulatory is harder for tooling than two separate tags finance, regulatory.
  • Keep tags small in number. A handful per element is plenty; long tag lists become noise.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: v0.8.0
kind: ObservabilityResults
id: 9f1c8a52-2b4e-4a6e-9d3e-7c2a1f0b4d11
observedAt: "2026-01-15T09:30:00Z"

source:
  process: nightly-quality-suite
results:
  - id: no_dup_rows
    type: check
    name: No duplicate rows
    status: pass
    tags: ['critical-path', 'uniqueness']

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Any string value in an OORS message MAY contain one or more variable references of the form ${VAR_NAME}, resolved at runtime by tooling. The mechanism is shared between all Bitol standards (RFC 0050, shared with ODCS and ODPS). It keeps environment-specific values — schema names, run identifiers, resource paths — out of the document itself.

References MAY appear as a whole value or as a substring. A reference MAY carry an inline default using the POSIX ${VAR_NAME:-default} form: the text between :- and the closing } is used verbatim when the variable is unset or empty.

VAR_NAME is an identifier chosen by the author. Resolution is intentionally left to tooling; common sources include OS environment variables, .env files, secret managers, and CI/CD pipeline variables.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
source:
  process: nightly-quality-suite
  runId: ${CI_PIPELINE_RUN_ID}
results:
  - id: no_dup_rows
    type: check
    name: No duplicate rows
    status: pass
    target:
      resourceType: table
      resourceIdentifier: ${DB_SCHEMA:-public}.orders

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: Form Behavior when the variable is set Behavior when the variable is unset or empty ${VAR_NAME} Replaced by the variable's value. Tooling SHOULD surface an error; it MUST NOT silently substitute an empty string. ${VAR_NAME:-default} Replaced by the variable's value. Replaced by default, verbatim.

docs.title: Tooling behavior
docs.text:
• Tools MUST resolve ${VAR_NAME} references before using the value for any purpose.
  • If a referenced variable cannot be resolved (and no default is supplied), tools SHOULD surface an error and MUST NOT silently substitute an empty string.
  • Tools MUST preserve unresolved ${VAR_NAME} and ${VAR_NAME:-default} tokens verbatim when serializing a message back to YAML or JSON (round-trip safety).
  • Tools MAY define their own resolution order across sources (for example, OS environment variable before .env file).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Interpolation applies to string values only: a field typed as a number, boolean, or a formatted string (such as the date-time observedAt) cannot hold an unresolved variable reference, as the schema rejects it.
  • No new section or field is added to the standard: a message using variables validates against the standard JSON schema as-is.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Complete OORS messages: a minimal example (only the required fields), a full example (every field), and a progressive example (an interim snapshot of a run still in progress — see Run Lifecycle), and a statuses example (all five results[].status outcomes — see Status values). Each is available in YAML and JSON, and validates against schema/oors-json-schema-v0.8.0.json.

Example YAML JSON Minimal — only required fields minimal.oors.yaml minimal.oors.json Full — every field, two results, contract & custom properties full.oors.yaml full.oors.json Progressive — interim snapshot (run.state: running) of a multi-step pipeline progressive.oors.yaml progressive.oors.json Variables — ${VAR_NAME} / ${VAR_NAME:-default} interpolation per RFC-0050 variables.oors.yaml variables.oors.json Statuses — all five results[].status outcomes (pass, fail, warn, error, skip) statuses.oors.yaml statuses.oors.json
